note: Hero subjects already used or reserved. The image-concept step must not reuse a subject, its main material or its setting. Seeded from docs/blog-image-prompts.md (reserved for the evergreen posts); each weekly run appends its chosen subject in its PR.

subjects.subject: A brass balance scale on dark slate, its two shallow pans holding different small objects, one pan resting slightly lower than the other.
Two fountain pens of clearly different design, one steel and one lacquered, lying crossed on dark grained leather.
Four vintage desk telephones lined up on a dark table, each from a different decade, handsets resting in their cradles.
A disassembled brass telescope eyepiece on dark felt, lens elements laid out in order beside the barrel.
A single coiled telephone switchboard patch cord with worn brass tips, resting on dark oiled wood.
The exposed brass movement of a clockwork orrery, gear teeth meshed, mainspring visible.
An open machinist's case with fitted foam cut-outs, three precision instruments seated exactly in their recesses and one recess empty.
A row of wooden-handled date stamps standing on a dark desk beside a well-used ink pad.
A 35mm contact sheet lying on a lightbox, strips of frames slightly overlapping, a loupe resting on one corner.
A steel pegboard wall with exactly six well-worn hand tools hung on it and many empty hooks around them.
A vintage telephone operator's switchboard with a small handful of cords patched across a field of unused jacks.
A folded engineering blueprint on a drafting table, revision marks in red pencil, an eraser and a scale rule beside it.
A worn leather tool roll unrolled on a bench, holding a deliberately small set of tools with empty loops between them.
A letterpress compositor's type case with metal sorts in their compartments, a few lifted out and resting on the frame.
A cutaway architectural section model on a dark table, its floor plates stacked and visibly separated.
A mechanical keyboard with several keycaps lifted off and set aside, bare switches exposed beneath.
Paper colour swatch fans opened and overlapping on a dark surface, with loose printed chips scattered across them.
A brass sextant resting on a folded nautical chart, dividers and a pencil alongside.
The carriage of a manual typewriter in close-up, a sheet of paper threaded through the platen.
A row of analogue mechanical kitchen timers of different sizes standing on a dark shelf.
A glass honesty jar half-filled with coins on a wooden counter, lid off and set beside it.
A 16mm film reel with a length of film unspooled across a lightbox, sprocket holes catching the light.
A darkroom enlarger head above an empty easel, developing trays waiting in the foreground shadow.
A library card catalogue drawer pulled fully open, cards fanned upright inside it.
A slide rule lying across a scattered stack of punched cards on dark felt.
A wooden pigeonhole letter rack, most slots stuffed with envelopes, a few empty.
A bundle of index cards tied with string beside a brass reading lamp casting a tight pool of light.
A steel planning board covered in small magnetic tiles arranged in staggered rows.
A large studio condenser microphone on a boom arm with a mesh pop filter just in front of it.
A hotel front-desk call bell on a marble counter, a rack of room keys on hooks behind it.
A sparse shelf holding four well-worn objects with wide gaps between them, everything else bare.
A set of machinist's precision gauge blocks stacked in a short tower on a steel surface.
The exposed brass mechanism of a clockwork automaton, linkages and cams visible through an open back panel.
An electronics workbench with an oscilloscope screen dark, a breadboard part-wired, and a soldering iron in its stand.
A dented brass megaphone lying on its side on a dark painted floor.
A grid of small instant-photo frames pinned to a dark corkboard, a few hanging slightly crooked.
A wooden schoolroom abacus with beads pushed to one side, worn chalk nubs resting beside it.
A half-thrown clay vessel on a potter's wheel, wet and asymmetric, trimmings scattered around the wheel head.
A drafting table with a T-square and set square laid over a sheet ruled in precise pencil lines.
A heavy steel door with the deadbolt thrown but the security chain hanging loose and unlatched.
An open desktop computer case lying on a workbench, a single large graphics card seated inside, dust and cable ties visible.
A brass gas meter with its dials in close-up, the housing scratched and the glass slightly clouded.
A stack of leather-bound legal volumes with cloth ribbon markers trailing from between the pages.
A stethoscope coiled on a stainless steel tray beside a monitor with a blank, unlit screen.
An overstuffed card catalogue with several drawers hanging open, identical cards spilling from them.
An empty glass and brass museum vitrine standing open on a dark floor, its velvet plinth bare.
A watering can spraying a wide scatter of droplets beside a single glass pipette releasing one precise drop.
A weathered wooden trail marker at the head of a long empty path, early morning light, the route stretching away.
A dusty stack of obsolete storage media, floppy disks, MiniDiscs and Zip cartridges, piled unevenly in a crate.
Stacks of Indian rupee coins of uneven height on a dark stone surface, three stacks far taller than the rest.
A government office rubber stamp resting on an open ledger beside a well-used purple ink pad.
A server rack seen through the mesh of its closed door, status lights small and dim in a darkened room.
A cutting-chai glass on a saucer beside a laptop on a crowded desk, condensation on the glass.
A plain cast-iron padlock clamped shut through an unfastened iron hasp, resting on a rough concrete slab with three loose bolts beside it.
